standards_reference: IPC-A-600 / IPC-6012 Industrial PCB Inspection Guidelines
disclaimer: AI advisory guidance only. Defect identification and classification originate from upstream visual inspection. The operator is responsible for final physical verification. This system does not independently approve or reject PCBs.

open_circuit.definition: A complete physical discontinuity or break along a conductive copper trace or via pad, interrupting electrical connection.
possible_consequences: Loss of signal continuity across the net, causing functional circuit failure.
Disconnected power rail or floating high-impedance logic input.
Intermittent operation under thermal expansion and mechanical vibration.
recommended_verification_procedure: Perform a two-point electrical continuity check using a calibrated digital multimeter (DMM) or flying probe tester across the affected net endpoints.
Inspect the break location under 10x-20x optical magnification with oblique lighting to confirm whether the copper is etched away or cracked.
Check adjacent layers/vias to determine if the break is isolated to the outer copper foil.
open_circuit.operator_guidance: Mark the bounding coordinates on the traveler sheet. Do not apply operational power to this board. Route the board to the rework station for micro-jumper review or flag for scrap according to IPC Class 2/3 acceptance criteria.

short_circuit.definition: An unintended conductive copper bridge, solder splash, or copper filament connecting two electrically distinct conductor traces or pads.
possible_consequences: Direct low-resistance path between distinct signals, ground, or power rails.
Severe overcurrent risk capable of damaging downstream integrated circuits or power supplies upon energization.
Nuisance tripping of power supply protection circuitry.
recommended_verification_procedure: Measure resistance across the affected nets with a digital multimeter to confirm near-zero ohm impedance before applying power.
Visually inspect under high magnification (15x-30x) to determine whether the bridge is surface copper foil, solder debris, or plating defect.
Verify trace clearance against the master PCB Gerber design rules.
short_circuit.operator_guidance: Immediately quarantine the PCB unit. Affix a DO NOT POWER warning label. Evaluate whether the bridge can be safely excised under a stereo microscope without violating dielectric base laminate integrity.

mouse_bite.definition: A notch, tear, or void along the edge of a copper conductor trace, reducing the effective cross-sectional conductor width.
possible_consequences: Localized current crowding and increased trace resistance at the bottleneck.
Elevated localized temperature rise (hotspot) under rated current load.
Vulnerability to fatigue fracture during thermal cycling or mechanical shock.
recommended_verification_procedure: Measure the remaining conductor width at the narrowest point of the notch using an optical measuring microscope or calibrated reticle.
Compare the measured width against IPC-A-600 criteria (conductor width reduction must typically not exceed 20% of nominal design width for Class 2/3).
Inspect surrounding base laminate for delamination or copper peel.
mouse_bite.operator_guidance: Record the remaining conductor percentage in the inspection log. If remaining width meets DRC specification, mark as acceptable defect condition; otherwise route to engineering lead for current-load review.

spur.definition: An unwanted sharp or irregular copper protrusion extending outward from a trace boundary into the adjacent dielectric spacing.
possible_consequences: Severe reduction of dielectric clearance distance to adjacent conductors.
Risk of electrical arc or dielectric breakdown during high-voltage transient events.
Potential trap for solder bridge formation during wave or reflow soldering.
recommended_verification_procedure: Measure the minimum remaining spacing between the spur apex and the nearest adjacent conductor under 20x magnification.
Verify whether remaining spacing satisfies IPC-A-600 minimum electrical clearance rules for the operating voltage class.
Examine whether the spur is firmly bonded to the base substrate or lifting.
spur.operator_guidance: Document the reduced clearance spacing. If clearance is less than design rule limits, evaluate for micro-trimming under magnification using an approved deburring tool.

spurious_copper.definition: An isolated, extraneous island, particle, or flake of unetched copper remaining in non-conductive dielectric areas.
possible_consequences: Violates minimum dielectric creepage and clearance specifications.
If poorly bonded, flake may dislodge during vibration and cause intermittent shorting elsewhere on the assembly.
Can cause high-frequency impedance anomalies or capacitive coupling.
recommended_verification_procedure: Inspect whether the copper flake is firmly bonded to the laminate or loose debris.
Measure the clearance distance between the spurious copper and all adjacent active nets.
Use an ESD-safe cleanroom swab with isopropyl alcohol to verify if it is loose particulate that can be safely wiped off.
spurious_copper.operator_guidance: If particulate is loose, clean thoroughly and re-inspect. If bonded copper flake violates electrical clearance rules, submit for MRB (Material Review Board) disposition.

pin_hole.definition: A small circular or irregular void, pit, or penetration within a conductive trace, pad, or ground plane surface.
possible_consequences: Slight reduction in conductor cross-section and localized resistance increase.
If located on an SMT solder pad or via annular ring, can degrade solder joint wetting and mechanical shear strength.
Trap for chemical residues, flux, or moisture, accelerating localized dendritic corrosion.
recommended_verification_procedure: Measure the void diameter relative to the total conductor width or pad area under 20x magnification.
Check compliance against IPC-A-600 void allowances (typically single voids <= 10% conductor width and not extending into conductor edge).
Inspect for corrosive contaminants inside the pit cavity.
pin_hole.operator_guidance: Determine if the pin hole is on a signal trace, power trace, or component pad. If on an SMT pad or exceeding 10% conductor reduction, mark for engineering sign-off; otherwise document and pass.
